A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same shopping-behavior simulation study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including material moved between appendices and main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, reasoning ablations, and action-distribution results on collected shopping sessions in Tables 1–2 and Figure 2.

after.justification: v5 retains those original empirical results and adds prompt-only model comparisons and an error-type analysis in Section 4.6 and Figure 3.

M1.justification: Both retain Claude-based reasoning synthesis, simplified HTML with hierarchical element names, three browser operations, context-masked next-token training, and reasoning-then-action generation. The expanded context description matches v1 Appendix B, and the supplied prompt templates are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use the same shopping dataset of 31,865 sessions, 3,526 users, and 230,965 actions for next-action generation and purchase-versus-termination prediction. Although v5 describes session-outcome classification as an additional task, it was already evaluated in v1. The HTML example and error analysis introduce no new evaluated domain or scenario.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add prompt-only counterparts for Qwen2.5 at 7B, 3B, and 1.5B; Mistral-7B-v0.3; and Llama 3.2 at 3B and 1B. These provide previously missing comparisons holding model family and size fixed. Figure 2 also replaces the row labeled Llama-3-1-8B with DeepSeek-R1.

E3.justification: The new error-analysis protocol defines five error categories and excludes illegal actions. Section 3.2 also changes the stated source of think-aloud examples from a couple of customers to one customer, without establishing that experiments were rerun. The retained evaluation procedure, metrics, 932 test cases, and training settings are unchanged; the 357-session count is newly disclosed.

E4.justification: v5 adds Section 4.6 and Figure 3, comparing Claude, DeepSeek-R1, and fine-tuned Qwen across missed termination, click, and search actions, incorrect search keywords, and incorrect clicked buttons. This substantially expands diagnosis beyond v1's action distributions and reasoning ablations. The existing reasoning ablation results are retained.

E5.justification: v1 provides no formal significance testing. v5 Section 4.4 introduces McNemar tests for central comparisons: p < 10^-10 for Qwen2.5-7B versus DeepSeek-R1 and p < 10^-5 for fine-tuned models versus their own prompt-only variants. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: All 22 existing Table 2 rows retain their numerical values, while six prompt-only rows are added. For example, Qwen2.5-7B receives newly reported prompt-only scores of 4.25% accuracy and 11.94% F1, alongside its retained fine-tuned 17.26% and 33.86%. Figure 2 substitutes DeepSeek-R1's distribution for the Llama row, and Figure 3 adds substantial failure-type results.

T1.justification: The formal history-to-reasoning-and-action mapping and shopping-session assumptions remain unchanged. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs, and v5 adds no mathematical derivation or formal property.

C1.justification: v5 drops the abstract's claim to establish a new benchmark and replaces the introduction's contribution language about realism and generalizability with behavioral fidelity. It foregrounds behavioral misalignment while retaining the principal claims of a first process-centric evaluation and benefits from fine-tuning with synthetic reasoning.

C2.justification: Sections 4.6 and 5.1 add substantive hypotheses linking excessive purchasing and failure to stop to task-completion objectives, and interpreting similar Claude/DeepSeek error profiles as shared training biases. They also connect realistic mistakes and search retries to UI/UX testing. These considerably extend v1's general discussion of fine-tuning and reasoning; the principal limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v5 Appendix B adds a concrete simplified-HTML context showing search inputs, filters, products, and pagination identifiers. Section 4.2 newly specifies 357 test sessions. Hardware and hyperparameters move from v1 Appendix A into Section 4.3 without changing, and the existing prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: v5 adds ReSpAct (Dongre et al., 2025), acknowledging conversational-agent reasoning datasets while distinguishing the human-behavior dataset gap. It also cites a second UXAgent paper, Lu et al. (2025b), in the usability-testing discussion. The broader positioning against prompt-only and outcome-centric approaches remains intact.

P1.justification: The title, author listing, abstract, and conclusion are revised. Context definitions and training details move from appendices into the main text, and the former discussion becomes a separate section with three subsections. The appendices are reorganized and Ethical Considerations becomes Limitations. Together these substantially restructure the presentation of retained material.

P2.justification: Figure 2 becomes a larger, full-width chart with percentage annotations and a reordered category legend; Figure 3 is added. Table 1 gains control rows and SFT labels, while Table 2 gains an explicit Setting column and wider layout. Figure 1 changes rationale labels to reasoning. Figure 3 incorrectly labels its count axis Percentage, and some captions retain outdated descriptions.

improvement.justification: v5 resolves an important control gap by adding prompt-only counterparts for all six fine-tuned models, substantially strengthening the central fine-tuning claim through comparisons holding model family and size fixed. The error analysis and significance reporting further strengthen the empirical assessment, while clearer organization and the HTML example improve transparency. Figure 3's mislabeled axis and stale captions are limited defects that do not outweigh the substantial improvement in experimental support.
